newsitem.title: USA: Profit-taking hits Agouron after run-up.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking hits Agouron after run-up.

text.p: Shares of high-flier Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc slipped in heavy trading on Wednesday, hit by profit-taking and a shift in coverage by a key institution.
Agouron shares fell 3 to close at 76-3/4. The stock had doubled from a level of around 50 in December to a high of 101 last month.
"People have made a lot of money on this stock, so when it starts to drop after such a wonderful run-up, they sell," said Edmund Debler, an analyst at Mehta & Isaly.

Analysts also suggested that the company's recent surge came as it developed its drug Viracept. Now that the anti-HIV drug is expected to be approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, sellers are emerging ahead of the news.

Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Robert LeBoyer said a very small number of floated shares, slight technical weakness and a secondary offering by rival Vertex Pharmaceuticals Inc might also be prompting investors to take profits.

"This stock hit my one-year price target in a month," he said. He also suggested that the recent move of key institutional analyst Doug Lind from PaineWebber to Morgan Stanley could also be weighing on the stock.

"Doug was one of their biggest supporters from early on and my expectation is that PaineWebber has a large retail network with a lot of Agouron shares in that network. Without Doug, and with such strong gains, the logical thing is to take some profits," he said.
Neither Lind nor Agouron Pharmaceuticals were immediately available for comment.
